notes.key_messages:
In order to do well in this examination, candidates should:
• write their answers as clearly as possible so that the meaning can be understood
• take care to include all the relevant details in their answers to questions in Exercise 4.
notes.general_comments:
Overall, candidates performed quite well in this examination and the full range of ability at IGCSE level was
seen. Most candidates attempted all the questions in the paper.
In this paper, credit is given for communication of the correct information. Answers are not assessed for the
accuracy of spelling and grammar. However, if language errors change the meaning or the meaning is
unclear, the answer cannot be credited.
Exercise 1
Questions 1–6
Most candidates gave the correct answers to all the questions in this exercise. Some candidates spelt
answers incorrectly in Question 2 and Question 3, and there were many variations of spelling seen. The
mark could only be awarded if the meaning could be understood.
Exercise 2
Questions 7 (i) – (viii)
Many candidates answered all the questions in this exercise correctly. A significant number of candidates
were unable to give the correct answer to sub-Questions iii, iv, and vi. To answer part iii correctly,
candidates needed to write the Hindi word for kite flying ‘Guddibazi’. In part iv many candidates were unable
to spell ‘darshanik’, the Hindi word for ‘philosopher’, and for part vi, the Hindi word ‘aaytakar’ was incorrect.
Exercise 3
Questions 8–13
Candidates seemed to be well prepared for this exercise and the majority of candidates responded very well
to the questions. A small number of weaker candidates seemed to be relying on guess work to answer the
questions in this exercise. Question 8 proved to be a good differentiator.
Exercise 4
Questions 14–20
In general, candidates made a good attempt to answer the questions in this exercise, but many were unable
to provide all the details required to score full marks. For most of the questions, more than one piece of
information needed to be given to form the complete correct answer. Although most candidates were able to
provide at least some of the details required, many candidates missed marks in this exercise by giving
incomplete answers to some or all of the questions.
0549 Hindi as a Second Language June 2014
In Question 14 (i) and (ii), candidates needed to include the Hindi words ‘people from Europe’, and for part
two, ‘ruling Arabs’. Many candidates did not answer in full, and therefore missed the mark.
For Question 15 (i), the complete answer required was ‘the ladies from the south who work in homes’. For
Part (ii) candidates needed to pick one from a variety of professions where Arabic is spoken, but some
candidates did not include the word ‘Arabic’ and hence lost the mark.
For Question 16 (ii), a large number of candidates failed to include the word ‘Hindi’ when giving their
theatre/poets/assemblies/films that people end up speaking English.
